subject: Review of Municipal Operations and Ballot Initiatives
overview: Former City Councilors Robert Penta and Michael Marks critiqued current municipal operations and discussed major ballot initiatives facing the city. The discussion focused on proposed zoning changes, charter reform, and the condition of public infrastructure and safety facilities.

items.title: Council Conduct and Public Participation
items.summary: Penta and Marks criticized the current council for reducing public speaking times and moving to a bi-weekly meeting schedule.

items.title: Proposed Zoning Recodification
items.summary: The guests expressed opposition to the elimination of single-family zoning districts, citing concerns over neighborhood density, traffic, and school capacity.

items.title: City Charter Review
items.summary: Marks supported the proposed charter's shift to ward representation, while Penta opposed the document due to the projected costs of adding council seats and the lack of council term limits.

items.title: High School Construction and Funding
items.summary: The discussion compared the necessity of building a new high school against the cost of refurbishing current facilities and maintaining elementary schools.

items.title: Infrastructure and Traffic Safety
items.summary: Speakers criticized recent street design elements like 'bump outs' and bike lanes while advocating for a dedicated budget to repave private ways.

items.title: Public Safety Facilities and Labor Contracts
items.summary: Marks and Penta advocated for the modernization of aging fire stations and more efficient negotiation of public safety contracts.
